# hubspot_dashboards (Data Source)

Lists HubSpot reporting dashboards matching optional filters (all filters combine with AND; within a set filter, any value matches). Typical use: snapshot every dashboard to git with `local_file` and `for_each` over the results, or feed `ids` into `import` blocks to adopt them as `hubspot_dashboard` resources. Every page of results is fetched (100 per request, following the pagination cursor).

`raw_json` holds the API object canonicalized — sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline — with the volatile view-tracking fields (`lastViewedAt`, `lastViewedByUserId`) stripped. It is meant for **committed snapshots** (write it with `local_file` and check it into git): a snapshot only diffs on real changes, and fields HubSpot adds to the API later are captured without a provider release. The typed `last_viewed_at` / `last_viewed_by_user_id` attributes still expose the view-tracking values.

**Report configuration (query, data sources, filters, visualization) is not exposed by the HubSpot API at all** — not even readable — so it cannot be captured here; only metadata, permissions, tags and dashboard layout are. Exporting report data (the API's emailed CSV/PDF export) is intentionally not offered: it is a side-effecting action on CRM record data, outside this provider's configuration-plane scope.

**The Analytics Reporting API is a public beta** (`/analytics/reporting/2027-03-beta`), so this is beta-backed per the provider's [API stability policy](https://github.com/revosai/terraform-provider-hubspot/blob/main/ROADMAP.md#api-stability-policy). The portal must opt into the beta (via the associated product update in HubSpot) and the token needs the `reporting.full.read` scope (plus `reporting.full.write` to create, clone or archive).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Snapshot every dashboard in the portal to git: one canonical JSON file per
# dashboard, keyed by ID. raw_json strips view-tracking fields, so a plan only
# shows a diff (and the repo only gets a commit) when a dashboard actually
# changed. Report configuration (query/visualization) is not exposed by the
# HubSpot API, so it cannot be part of the snapshot.
data "hubspot_dashboards" "all" {
  # Also capture widget layout and the reports on each dashboard.
  include_widgets = true
}

resource "local_file" "dashboard_snapshot" {
  for_each = { for d in data.hubspot_dashboards.all.dashboards : d.id => d }

  filename = "${path.module}/reporting/dashboards/${each.key}.json"
  content  = each.value.raw_json
}

# Filters combine with AND; within a set filter any value matches.
data "hubspot_dashboards" "sales_team" {
  query          = "sales" # name or description contains "sales"
  owner_user_ids = ["1234567", "7654321"]
}

output "sales_team_dashboard_ids" {
  value = data.hubspot_dashboards.sales_team.ids
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `archived` (Boolean) When `true`, returns archived dashboards **instead of** active ones (mirrors the API's `archived` parameter). Defaults to `false`.
- `business_unit_ids` (Set of String) Only dashboards in one of these business units (`0` is the default business unit).
- `include_widgets` (Boolean) When `true`, also requests each dashboard's widgets, populating `widgets` and `report_ids` and including `widgets` in each `raw_json` (which then equals the `hubspot_dashboard` data source's `raw_json`). Defaults to `false`: widgets are not requested, `widgets` / `report_ids` are null and `raw_json` has no `widgets` key.
- `owner_user_ids` (Set of String) Only dashboards owned by one of these HubSpot user IDs.
- `query` (String) Only dashboards whose name **or description** contains this text (case-insensitive, HubSpot's `q` search).
- `tag_ids` (Set of String) Only dashboards carrying at least one of these tag IDs.

### Read-Only

- `dashboards` (Attributes List) The matching dashboards, ordered by ascending numeric ID. Each item has the same attributes as the `hubspot_dashboard` data source, including its own `raw_json` snapshot. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dashboards))
- `id` (String) Stable identifier for this data source: `dashboards`, followed by the non-default filter arguments as a sorted, URL-encoded query string (e.g. `dashboards?query=sales`).
- `ids` (List of String) IDs of the matching dashboards, in result order (ascending numeric ID).

<a id="nestedatt--dashboards"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dashboards`

Read-Only:

- `archived` (Boolean) Whether the dashboard is archived.
- `archived_at` (String) When the dashboard was archived (ISO 8601); null for an active dashboard.
- `business_unit_id` (String) Business unit (brand) the dashboard belongs to; `0` is the default business unit.
- `created_at` (String) When the dashboard was created (ISO 8601).
- `created_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the dashboard's creator.
- `description` (String) The dashboard's description (null when unset).
- `id` (String) The dashboard's ID.
- `last_viewed_at` (String) When the dashboard was last viewed (ISO 8601). Volatile — it changes whenever anyone opens the dashboard — so it is excluded from `raw_json`.
- `last_viewed_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the last viewer. Volatile; excluded from `raw_json`.
- `name` (String) The dashboard's name.
- `owner_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the dashboard's owner.
- `permissions` (Attributes) Who can access the dashboard. `type` is one of `PRIVATE`, `EVERYONE_VIEW`, `EVERYONE_EDIT` or `SPECIFIC`; with `SPECIFIC`, list the users/teams in `view` and/or `edit`. Grants are sets (order-insensitive) and are only allowed with `SPECIFIC`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dashboards--permissions))
- `raw_json` (String) The full API dashboard object as canonical JSON for committed snapshots: sorted keys, 2-space indent, trailing newline, view-tracking fields (`lastViewedAt`, `lastViewedByUserId`) stripped.
- `report_ids` (List of String) Distinct IDs of the reports shown on the dashboard's widgets, sorted. Null unless the data source sets `include_widgets = true`.
- `tags` (Attributes List) Tags on the dashboard (read-only: the API cannot set tags). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dashboards--tags))
- `updated_at` (String) When the dashboard was last updated (ISO 8601).
- `updated_by_user_id` (String) HubSpot user ID of the user who last updated the dashboard.
- `widgets` (Attributes List) Widgets on the dashboard with their grid layout (read-only: the API cannot position widgets). Null unless the data source sets `include_widgets = true`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dashboards--widgets))

<a id="nestedatt--dashboards--permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dashboards.permissions`

Read-Only:

- `edit` (Attributes Set) Users/teams granted edit access to the dashboard (`SPECIFIC` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dashboards--permissions--edit))
- `type` (String) Permission type.
- `view` (Attributes Set) Users/teams granted view access to the dashboard (`SPECIFIC` only). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dashboards--permissions--view))

<a id="nestedatt--dashboards--permissions--edit"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dashboards.permissions.edit`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) HubSpot user ID or team ID.
- `type` (String) Grantee kind: `USER` or `TEAM`.


<a id="nestedatt--dashboards--permissions--view"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dashboards.permissions.view`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) HubSpot user ID or team ID.
- `type` (String) Grantee kind: `USER` or `TEAM`.



<a id="nestedatt--dashboards--tags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dashboards.tags`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String) Tag ID.
- `name` (String) Tag name.


<a id="nestedatt--dashboards--widgets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dashboards.widgets`

Read-Only:

- `height` (Number) Widget height in grid units.
- `report_id` (String) ID of the report the widget shows.
- `width` (Number) Widget width in grid units.
- `x` (Number) 0-based horizontal grid position.
- `y` (Number) 0-based vertical grid position.
